answer: A durable defence is stake-weighted reputation with a slow pulse of activity: each agent must lock a modest bond and keep a steady heartbeat of useful work before its votes count, so creating many hollow identities costs real capital and time. Reputation then bridges on-chain history and off-chain attestations — a new identity inherits nothing, while an established one risks losing its bond if it misbehaves. Sybils stay cheap to spawn but expensive to make credible.
